note: One expectation index per contract directory. Each case names the structural violations that prove its point as (pointer, keyword) pairs; a validator's free-text message is deliberately never recorded. The expected set must be a subset of what the validator reports, because a conditional rule often reports a broader violation alongside the specific one.

provider-failure-with-negative-polarity.proves: The rule this whole slice exists for: a provider that failed cannot be reported as a negative finding about the website. The polarity member is refused outright rather than set to some neutral token, so there is no value a careless writer could reach for.

runtime-error-with-polarity.proves: The same rule for our own runtime: a crash inside the analysis says nothing about the analysed site, and the contract will not let it say anything.

timeout-with-polarity.proves: A timeout carries no polarity either, and not even a POSITIVE one: the ban is on stating a website judgement without an assessment, not merely on stating a bad one.

unknown-with-negative-polarity.proves: An assessment that ran but established nothing is still not a finding. UNKNOWN is the honest outcome of a performed observation, and it may not be silently read as a defect.

conflict-with-negative-polarity.proves: Conflicting observations are a state of the evidence, not a verdict on the site. Resolving a conflict is a later decision that must be taken deliberately rather than defaulted to NEGATIVE here.

not-applicable-with-negative-polarity.proves: A measurement that does not apply to this subject cannot count against it. NOT_APPLICABLE lives in result_state, so it never has to be smuggled in as a polarity value.

polarity-neutral.proves: The polarity vocabulary is closed at POSITIVE and NEGATIVE. There is deliberately no NEUTRAL token: a KNOWN observation that carries no judgement omits the member instead, so nobody has to invent what neutral would mean.

known-without-measurement-reference.proves: KNOWN website evidence is derived evidence: it must name at least one measurement record it came from, so no claim about the site exists without something measured behind it.

assessment-both-groups.proves: Evidence cannot claim both that it was observed and that it was never assessed, by the same structural rule the measurement record applies to itself.

inline-raw-response-body.proves: A captured response body never lives inline in normalised evidence. The closed root refuses the member, so raw provider data cannot travel with the evidence into every downstream consumer.

scenario-lowercase.proves: The scenario vocabulary is open but not free text: it keeps a stable upper-snake shape, so a scenario a later slice introduces stays a token rather than prose.
